about: Massican is the white-wine-only label Dan Petroski founded in Napa Valley in 2009, which made it an outlier in a valley built on Cabernet. Petroski left a career in magazine publishing to live in Italy, fell for the whites of Friuli and Campania, and came back to California to learn winemaking from the ground up. The name honours his family: his great-grandfather grew up in the foothills of Monte Massico, north of Naples. Massican owns no vineyards and buys from growers; in 2023 E. & J. Gallo acquired the brand, with Petroski staying on as winemaker.

Pinot Grigio joined the lineup after the Gallo partnership opened up new fruit sources, and Petroski models it on the Pinot Grigio of Collio rather than the mass-market Italian style. The 2024 comes from cool sites in Sonoma and Lodi and is mostly Pinot Grigio with about a fifth Cortese, the grape of Gavi. It is fermented in neutral oak barrels and large foudres, and like all Massican wines it is made without malolactic fermentation, aiming for freshness and moderate alcohol.

The winery describes it as a dry, pre-dinner white of fresh flowers, citrus, sea salt and almonds, meant for early-evening snacks but sturdy enough to carry on to the table. Cortese adds a crisp, saline edge to Pinot Grigio’s gentle fruit, and neutral oak is used for texture rather than oak flavour. At about 13 percent alcohol, it is in keeping with Massican’s long-standing preference for whites that stay fresh and food-friendly rather than big and ripe.
